posts.caption:
Last look for the incredible shoot with @caracormack_ . I wanted to have a back up wig for our female bodybuilder so I dashed to Paks for a cheap blonde wig. The only one in budget was straight and didn’t have much volume. I took it home and using Velcro rollers put a set in the hair. I put the wig under a plastic bag and steamed the wig for a couple of minutes. Left it to dry and when I took the rollers out I had bouncy curls. I then back combed the life out of it and also put a bit of root in using colour mousse sprays so it looked a bit more realistic and less cheap. A tonne of Bastiste took the shine off. Keep swiping to see my terrible pics of the process. Must get better at this!  Creative Direction/ Photography @caracormack_

posts.caption:
HOT STUFF! The dreamy @caracormack_ had a vision for this incredible shoot supported by @malibu_rum.
To create this look I made several stencils out of acetate that I cut out with a craft knife. I didn’t know exactly how big our bodybuilder @elliott_minnet’s back was going to be and it needed to be the right size. I then airbrushed tan makeup and also my favourite Sunburn spray in Pinky by Maekup over the stencil, let it dry and then voila! Then we followed that with a spritz of baby oil mixed in with water. I also put a cheeky tan line near his bathers. I sourced the wig from @am_thewigstore. Thank you so much to Kelly for your help. The wig was steamed with some rollers in to create some movement.  Creative Direction/ Photography @caracormack_

posts.caption:
When @samuel_hicks_ asked if I wanted to do a shoot based on scenes in Tokyo, I jumped at the chance. Sadly we shot this in a London studio and the backgrounds were digitally crafted. I did however get the chance to do what I love best which is to create some characters, using amongst other things some tattoos. Check out @scarletmayrobinson hands on the first image.  Sam was inspired by the paintings of Keita Morimoto, who portrays moments of urban life with cinematic flair. They evoke the grade and use of light of Tod Hido and Gregory Crewdson, yet they focus more on everyday moments in cities like Tokyo. 
Sam set out to create a series of images taken at twilight, the time when street and neon lights start to dominate the atmosphere. His aim was to capture people and urban scenes resembling moments from a film. Recently, when Sam showed some of these images to a friend from Tokyo, she remarked that they looked like they were shot in “kiri.” In Japanese, “kiri” means mist or fog. This misty, dream-like quality of “kiri” aligns perfectly with the mood that Sam wanted to evoke.
These portraits were photographed with real people in London and paired with digitally crafted backgrounds. Casting by @camillaarthurcasting, styling by @charlottelouiseholt, retouch by @stanleys_post, production by @killer_art_production @scarletmayrobinson on modelling
